answer: With 500 abstracts per domain under condition C, both rank-frequency curves remain Zipf-like: k = 1.125 (R² 0.961) for GLP-1 (medical) and k = 1.038 (R² 0.949) for Computer science (arXiv), a difference of 0.086. The overall shape is therefore similar, but the details are domain-specific. GLP-1 (medical) has 12,626 distinct terms versus 13,001 for Computer science (arXiv) (49.7% vs 51.4% hapax), and only 17.3% of the combined vocabulary is shared. The top-10 lists share 0 terms (none); the other head terms name each domain's subject (glp-1, receptor, patients, weight, metabolic, obesity, risk, agonists, diabetes, outcomes vs model, models, across, data, language, two, show, training, framework, results). Domain specificity thus changes which terms occupy the head and how large the tail is, while the heavy-tailed form persists. Two single-topic samples cannot establish a general effect size; the exponent also depends on preprocessing and the fitted rank range.
